This notebook reproduces the simulations behind Lecture 10 and leaves you four short problems. The slides use
`rdd_sims.R` (in this folder), which runs the same simulations with more plotting. Everything is simulated, so you
always know the right answer. You need `rdrobust` and `rddensity` from CRAN.

# Part 1: The sharp design

## Reproduce: SOX Section 404 at the \$75M threshold

Accelerated filers (public float of at least \$75M) needed an auditor attestation of internal controls from fiscal
2004. The running variable is $x = \log(\text{float}/\$75\text{M})$, so the cutoff is $x = 0$. The outcome is the
fiscal 2004 log audit fee. Without SOX, audit fees rise smoothly but non-linearly with size; `curv` scales the
curvature. The true jump is $\tau = 0.35$. We also record fiscal 2002 fees, before SOX existed.

```{r}
tau <- 0.35
f0 <- function(x, curv = 1) 11 + 0.5 * x + curv * 0.3 * tanh(2.5 * x)
sim_sox <- function(N = 4000, curv = 1) {
  x <- rnorm(N, 0, 1.2)
  u <- rnorm(N, 0, 0.25)                        # persistent audit-cost shifter
  D <- as.integer(x >= 0)
  data.frame(x = x, u = u, D = D,
             y = f0(x, curv) + tau * D + u + rnorm(N, 0, 0.2),
             y_pre = f0(x, curv) - 0.06 + u + rnorm(N, 0, 0.2))
}
d <- sim_sox()
rdplot(d$y, d$x, c = 0, x.label = "log(float / $75M)", y.label = "log audit fee")
```

Global polynomials (separate on each side) against local linear regression:

```{r}
global_poly <- function(d, p) coef(feols(as.formula(sprintf("y ~ D * poly(x, %d, raw = TRUE)", p)), d))["D"]
sapply(1:5, function(p) global_poly(d, p))

rd <- rdrobust(d$y, d$x, c = 0)
summary(rd)
h <- rd$bws["h", "left"]
s <- subset(d, abs(x) < h); s$k <- 1 - abs(s$x) / h
etable(feols(y ~ D * x, s, weights = ~k, vcov = "hetero"))   # coefficient on D = rdrobust's "Conventional"
```

## Reproduce: coverage of conventional vs. robust bias-corrected CIs

```{r}
mc <- function(R = 200, N = 4000, curv = 1) {
  out <- t(replicate(R, {
    s <- sim_sox(N, curv); r <- rdrobust(s$y, s$x)
    c(conv = r$ci[1, 1] <= tau & tau <= r$ci[1, 2], robust = r$ci[3, 1] <= tau & tau <= r$ci[3, 2], h = r$bws[1, 1])
  }))
  colMeans(out)
}
mc()
```

# Part 2: Manipulation

## Reproduce: float management

Firms whose true float is between \$75M and \$96M ($0 \le x < 0.25$) may push their reported float just under
\$75M to stay exempt. Firms with higher audit costs $u$ are more likely to do it; `sel` sets how strongly
manipulation selects on $u$. Manipulators stay exempt but keep the audit fees of their true size and costs.

```{r}
manipulate <- function(d, sel = 8, base = -0.5) {
  cand <- which(d$x >= 0 & d$x < 0.25)
  m <- cand[runif(length(cand)) < plogis(base + sel * d$u[cand])]
  d$x[m] <- runif(length(m), -0.12, -0.005); d$D[m] <- 0L; d$y[m] <- d$y[m] - tau
  d
}
dm <- manipulate(d)
hist(dm$x[abs(dm$x) < 1], breaks = seq(-1, 1, by = 0.04), main = "Reported float", xlab = "x")
abline(v = 0, lty = 2)

c(density_p = rddensity(dm$x)$test$p_jk,
  jump_2004 = rdrobust(dm$y, dm$x)$coef[1],
  jump_2002 = rdrobust(dm$y_pre, dm$x)$coef[1])
```

# Part 3: Fuzzy RD

## Reproduce: voluntary compliers and extensions

Now crossing \$75M only raises the probability of an attestation. Low-cost firms are more likely to attest on
either side. `fs` sets how much crossing the cutoff matters.

```{r}
fuzzy <- function(d, fs = 2.4) {
  d$Z <- as.integer(d$x >= 0)
  d$D <- as.integer(-1.3 + fs * d$Z - 4 * d$u + rnorm(nrow(d)) > 0)
  d$y <- f0(d$x) + tau * d$D + d$u + rnorm(nrow(d), 0, 0.2)
  d
}
df <- fuzzy(d)
rf <- rdrobust(df$y, df$x, fuzzy = df$D)
h <- rf$bws["h", "left"]; s <- subset(df, abs(x) < h); s$k <- 1 - abs(s$x) / h
etable(feols(D ~ Z * x, s, weights = ~k, vcov = "hetero"),            # first stage
       feols(y ~ Z * x, s, weights = ~k, vcov = "hetero"),            # reduced form
       feols(y ~ x + Z:x | D ~ Z, s, weights = ~k, vcov = "hetero"))  # 2SLS = Wald ratio
summary(rf)
```
